title: Preventive Dental Care: Everyday Habits for a Healthier Smile
description: Discover simple preventive dental care tips for healthy teeth and gums, from daily brushing and flossing to regular dental checkups.
headline: Simple Habits for Preventive Dental Care

featuredImage.alt: Preventive dental care at West End Dental Centre in Edmonton

body:
Preventive dental care is one of the most important parts of maintaining a healthy smile. While dental treatment can help address problems when they arise, regular checkups and good daily habits can help reduce the risk of cavities, gum disease, and other oral health concerns.

From brushing and flossing to professional cleanings and a balanced diet, small steps can make a meaningful difference over time.

Here are some of the most common questions patients have about preventive and everyday dental care.

How often should you visit the dentist?

For many patients, regular dental examinations and professional cleanings are recommended approximately every six months. However, the right schedule can vary depending on your individual oral health needs.

Some patients may benefit from more frequent visits, particularly if they have a history of gum disease, frequent cavities, dental restorations, or other oral health concerns.

Your dental team can recommend an appointment schedule based on your teeth, gums, medical history, and overall oral health. Regular visits allow your dentist to monitor changes and identify concerns that may not yet be causing noticeable symptoms.

What happens during a dental cleaning?

A professional dental cleaning helps remove plaque and hardened deposits, known as tartar or calculus, from areas that can be difficult to clean effectively at home.

During a cleaning, your dental hygienist may:

  • Examine your gums and overall oral health
  • Remove plaque and tartar from around the teeth and gumline
  • Clean between the teeth
  • Polish the teeth
  • Review brushing and flossing techniques
  • Provide recommendations based on your individual needs

Professional cleanings work together with your daily home-care routine to help maintain healthy teeth and gums.

Why do my gums bleed when I brush?

Occasional gum bleeding may happen for several reasons, but gums that regularly bleed during brushing or flossing should not be ignored.

One common cause is inflammation related to plaque buildup around the gumline. This early stage of gum disease is often referred to as gingivitis.

Other possible causes may include brushing too aggressively, changes in your flossing routine, certain medications, or other oral health conditions.

If your gums regularly bleed, feel swollen, or are tender, a dental examination can help determine the cause.

How should you brush and floss properly?

Good oral hygiene begins with a consistent routine.

Most people should brush their teeth twice a day using a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste. Brush gently along the gumline and make sure to clean the front, back, and chewing surfaces of each tooth.

Avoid brushing too aggressively, as excessive pressure may irritate the gums or contribute to tooth sensitivity over time.

Cleaning between your teeth is also important because a toothbrush cannot always reach these areas effectively. Floss, interdental brushes, water flossers, or other recommended cleaning tools can help remove plaque and food debris between teeth and around the gumline.

Your dental team can help you determine which tools and techniques work best for you.

Why do regular dental checkups matter?

Some dental concerns can develop without causing immediate pain or discomfort.

Regular dental examinations give your dentist an opportunity to monitor your oral health and look for signs of:

  • Tooth decay
  • Gum disease
  • Cracked or damaged teeth
  • Worn dental restorations
  • Changes in your bite
  • Signs of teeth grinding
  • Changes in the tissues of your mouth

Identifying concerns earlier may allow for more treatment options and can sometimes prevent a minor issue from developing into a more significant problem.

What causes bad breath?

Occasional bad breath is common, especially after eating certain foods. Persistent bad breath, however, may sometimes be related to an oral health concern.

Common causes can include:

  • Plaque and bacteria buildup
  • Gum disease
  • Food trapped between teeth
  • Dry mouth
  • Smoking or vaping
  • Certain foods and beverages
  • Cavities or dental infections
  • Some medical conditions or medications

Good brushing, cleaning between the teeth, and cleaning the tongue can help reduce bacteria that contribute to bad breath. If bad breath persists despite good oral hygiene, speak with your dentist so they can help determine whether there may be an underlying cause.

How often should you replace your toothbrush?

A toothbrush or electric toothbrush head should generally be replaced every three to four months. You may need to replace it sooner if the bristles become frayed, bent, or worn.

Worn bristles may not clean the teeth as effectively and can make it more difficult to remove plaque along the gumline.

You may also want to replace your toothbrush after certain illnesses, particularly if recommended by your healthcare or dental provider.

What is plaque and why does it matter?

Plaque is a sticky film of bacteria that continuously forms on your teeth.

When plaque is not removed through brushing and cleaning between the teeth, it can contribute to cavities and gum inflammation.

Over time, some plaque can harden into tartar or calculus. Unlike plaque, tartar cannot usually be removed through regular brushing and requires professional dental cleaning.

A consistent home-care routine combined with professional dental visits can help control plaque buildup.

How does diet affect your teeth?

What you eat and drink can affect your oral health.

Foods and beverages that are high in sugar or carbohydrates can provide fuel for bacteria in the mouth. These bacteria produce acids that can contribute to tooth decay.

Frequent snacking or sipping on sugary drinks throughout the day may expose the teeth to repeated acid attacks.

To help support your oral health:

  • Drink water regularly
  • Limit frequent sugary snacks and beverages
  • Choose balanced meals
  • Include nutrient-rich foods such as vegetables, fruits, dairy products, proteins, and whole grains
  • Avoid frequently sipping sugary or acidic drinks throughout the day

You do not necessarily have to avoid your favourite foods entirely. Frequency, portion size, and your overall dental care routine all play a role.

Dental care tips for busy families

Keeping everyone in the family on top of their oral health can sometimes feel challenging, particularly with busy school, work, and activity schedules.

A few simple habits can make dental care easier:

  • Keep toothbrushes and toothpaste somewhere easy to access
  • Establish consistent morning and bedtime brushing routines
  • Schedule family dental appointments in advance
  • Keep floss or other interdental cleaning tools visible as a reminder
  • Encourage children to brush for approximately two minutes
  • Pack water instead of sugary drinks when possible
  • Replace everyone's toothbrushes at the same time every few months
  • Address tooth pain or other dental concerns rather than waiting for the next scheduled visit

Building oral health into your family's everyday routine can make preventive care feel more manageable.

Prevention starts with small habits

Good oral health does not depend on one single habit. It is the combination of daily brushing and flossing, healthy food choices, professional cleanings, and regular dental examinations that helps protect your smile over time.

Your dental needs can also change throughout your life, which is why maintaining an ongoing relationship with your dental team is important.
